paragraphs.text: Finally, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed is not irksome, but for you it is safe.
paragraphs.original: Τὸ λοιπόν, ἀδελφοί μου, χαίρετε ἐν κυρίῳ. τὰ αὐτὰ γράφειν ὑμῖν ἐμοὶ μὲν οὐκ ὀκνηρόν, ὑμῖν δὲ ἀσφαλές.
paragraphs.translit: To loipon, adelphoi mou, chairete en kyriō. ta auta graphein hymin emoi men ouk oknēron, hymin de asphales.

paragraphs.text: Beware of the dogs, beware of the evil workers, beware of the concision:
paragraphs.original: Βλέπετε τοὺς κύνας, βλέπετε τοὺς κακοὺς ἐργάτας, βλέπετε τὴν κατατομήν.
paragraphs.translit: Blepete tous kynas, blepete tous kakous ergatas, blepete tēn katatomēn.

paragraphs.text: for we are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God, and glory in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh:
paragraphs.original: ἡμεῖς γάρ ἐσμεν ἡ περιτομή, οἱ πνεύματι θεοῦ λατρεύοντες καὶ καυχώμενοι ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐν σαρκὶ πεποιθότες,
paragraphs.translit: hēmeis gar esmen hē peritomē, hoi pneumati theou latreuontes kai kauchōmenoi en Christō Iēsou kai ouk en sarki pepoithotes,

paragraphs.text: though I myself might have confidence even in the flesh: if any other man thinketh to have confidence in the flesh, I yet more:
paragraphs.original: καίπερ ἐγὼ ἔχων πεποίθησιν καὶ ἐν σαρκί. Εἴ τις δοκεῖ ἄλλος πεποιθέναι ἐν σαρκί, ἐγὼ μᾶλλον·
paragraphs.translit: kaiper egō echōn pepoithēsin kai en sarki. Ei tis dokei allos pepoithenai en sarki, egō mallon·

paragraphs.text: circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee;
paragraphs.original: περιτομῇ ὀκταήμερος, ἐκ γένους Ἰσραήλ, φυλῆς Βενιαμίν, Ἑβραῖος ἐξ Ἑβραίων, κατὰ νόμον Φαρισαῖος,
paragraphs.translit: peritomē oktaēmeros, ek genous Israēl, phylēs Beniamin, Hebraios ex Hebraiōn, kata nomon Pharisaios,

paragraphs.text: as touching zeal, persecuting the church; as touching the righteousness which is in the law, found blameless.
paragraphs.original: κατὰ ζῆλος διώκων τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, κατὰ δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐν νόμῳ γενόμενος ἄμεμπτος.
paragraphs.translit: kata zēlos diōkōn tēn ekklēsian, kata dikaiosynēn tēn en nomō genomenos amemptos.

paragraphs.text: Howbeit what things were gain to me, these have I counted loss for Christ.
paragraphs.original: Ἀλλὰ ἅτινα ἦν μοι κέρδη, ταῦτα ἥγημαι διὰ τὸν Χριστὸν ζημίαν.
paragraphs.translit: Alla hatina ēn moi kerdē, tauta hēgēmai dia ton Christon zēmian.

paragraphs.text: Yea verily, and I count all things to be loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but refuse, that I may gain Christ,
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ μενοῦνγε καὶ ἡγοῦμαι πάντα ζημίαν εἶναι διὰ τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ κυρίου μου διʼ ὃν τὰ πάντα ἐζημιώθην, καὶ ἡγοῦμαι σκύβαλα ἵνα Χριστὸν κερδήσω
paragraphs.translit: alla menounge kai hēgoumai panta zēmian einai dia to hyperechon tēs gnōseōs Christou Iēsou tou kyriou mou diʼ hon ta panta ezēmiōthēn, kai hēgoumai skybala hina Christon kerdēsō

paragraphs.text: and be found in him, not having a righteousness of mine own, [even] that which is of the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness which is from God by faith:
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὑρεθῶ ἐν αὐτῷ, μὴ ἔχων ἐμὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐκ νόμου ἀλλὰ τὴν διὰ πίστεως Χριστοῦ, τὴν ἐκ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει,
paragraphs.translit: kai heurethō en autō, mē echōn emēn dikaiosynēn tēn ek nomou alla tēn dia pisteōs Christou, tēn ek theou dikaiosynēn epi tē pistei,

paragraphs.text: that I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, becoming conformed unto his death;
paragraphs.original: τοῦ γνῶναι αὐτὸν καὶ τὴν δύναμιν τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ καὶ κοινωνίαν παθημάτων αὐτοῦ, συμμορφιζόμενος τῷ θανάτῳ αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: tou gnōnai auton kai tēn dynamin tēs anastaseōs autou kai koinōnian pathēmatōn autou, symmorphizomenos tō thanatō autou,

paragraphs.text: if by any means I may attain unto the resurrection from the dead.
paragraphs.original: εἴ πως καταντήσω εἰς τὴν ἐξανάστασιν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ei pōs katantēsō eis tēn exanastasin tēn ek nekrōn.

paragraphs.text: Not that I have already obtained, or am already made perfect: but I press on, if so be that I may lay hold on that for which also I was laid hold on by Christ Jesus.
paragraphs.original: Οὐχ ὅτι ἤδη ἔλαβον ἢ ἤδη τετελείωμαι, διώκω δὲ εἰ καὶ καταλάβω, ἐφʼ ᾧ καὶ κατελήμφθην ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Ouch hoti ēdē elabon ē ēdē teteleiōmai, diōkō de ei kai katalabō, ephʼ hō kai katelēmphthēn hypo Christou.

paragraphs.text: Brethren, I could not myself yet to have laid hold: but one thing [I do], forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before,
paragraphs.original: ἀδελφοί, ἐγὼ ἐμαυτὸν οὐ λογίζομαι κατειληφέναι· ἓν δέ, τὰ μὲν ὀπίσω ἐπιλανθανόμενος τοῖς δὲ ἔμπροσθεν ἐπεκτεινόμενος,
paragraphs.translit: adelphoi, egō emauton ou logizomai kateilēphenai· hen de, ta men opisō epilanthanomenos tois de emprosthen epekteinomenos,

paragraphs.text: I press on toward the goal unto the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
paragraphs.original: κατὰ σκοπὸν διώκω εἰς τὸ βραβεῖον τῆς ἄνω κλήσεως τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kata skopon diōkō eis to brabeion tēs anō klēseōs tou theou en Christō Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: Let us therefore, as many as are perfect, be thus minded: and if in anything ye are otherwise minded, this also shall God reveal unto you:
paragraphs.original: ὅσοι οὖν τέλειοι, τοῦτο φρονῶμεν· καὶ εἴ τι ἑτέρως φρονεῖτε, καὶ τοῦτο ὁ θεὸς ὑμῖν ἀποκαλύψει·
paragraphs.translit: hosoi oun teleioi, touto phronōmen· kai ei ti heterōs phroneite, kai touto ho theos hymin apokalypsei·

paragraphs.text: only, whereunto we have attained, by that same [rule] let us walk.
paragraphs.original: πλὴν εἰς ὃ ἐφθάσαμεν, τῷ αὐτῷ στοιχεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: plēn eis ho ephthasamen, tō autō stoichein.

paragraphs.text: Brethren, be ye imitators together of me, and mark them that so walk even as ye have us for an ensample.
paragraphs.original: Συμμιμηταί μου γίνεσθε, ἀδελφοί, καὶ σκοπεῖτε τοὺς οὕτω περιπατοῦντας καθὼς ἔχετε τύπον ἡμᾶς·
paragraphs.translit: Symmimētai mou ginesthe, adelphoi, kai skopeite tous houtō peripatountas kathōs echete typon hēmas·

paragraphs.text: For many walk, of whom I told you often, and now tell you even weeping, [that they are] the enemies of the cross of Christ:
paragraphs.original: πολλοὶ γὰρ περιπατοῦσιν οὓς πολλάκις ἔλεγον ὑμῖν, νῦν δὲ καὶ κλαίων λέγω, τοὺς ἐχθροὺς τοῦ σταυροῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: polloi gar peripatousin hous pollakis elegon hymin, nyn de kai klaiōn legō, tous echthrous tou staurou tou Christou,

paragraphs.text: whose end is perdition, whose god is the belly, and [whose] glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.
paragraphs.original: ὧν τὸ τέλος ἀπώλεια, ὧν ὁ θεὸς ἡ κοιλία καὶ ἡ δόξα ἐν τῇ αἰσχύνῃ αὐτῶν, οἱ τὰ ἐπίγεια φρονοῦντες.
paragraphs.translit: hōn to telos apōleia, hōn ho theos hē koilia kai hē doxa en tē aischynē autōn, hoi ta epigeia phronountes.

paragraphs.text: For our citizenship is in heaven; whence also we wait for a Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ:
paragraphs.original: ἡμῶν γὰρ τὸ πολίτευμα ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὑπάρχει, ἐξ οὗ καὶ σωτῆρα ἀπεκδεχόμεθα κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν,
paragraphs.translit: hēmōn gar to politeuma en ouranois hyparchei, ex hou kai sōtēra apekdechometha kyrion Iēsoun Christon,

paragraphs.text: who shall fashion anew the body of our humiliation, [that it may be] conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working whereby he is able even to subject all things unto himself.
paragraphs.original: ὃς μετασχηματίσει τὸ σῶμα τῆς ταπεινώσεως ἡμῶν σύμμορφον τῷ σώματι τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ δύνασθαι αὐτὸν καὶ ὑποτάξαι αὑτῷ τὰ πάντα.
paragraphs.translit: hos metaschēmatisei to sōma tēs tapeinōseōs hēmōn symmorphon tō sōmati tēs doxēs autou kata tēn energeian tou dynasthai auton kai hypotaxai hautō ta panta.
